faq.q: Are there boy jobs and girl jobs?
faq.a: No. Any job can be done by anyone who has the skills and interest. Some jobs have more men or more women today, mostly because of history and stereotypes, not ability.
asks: Are some jobs only for boys?

faq.a: A gender stereotype is a fixed idea about what boys or girls, or men or women, should like or do, like "girls are not good at building" or "boys do not cry". It ignores that everyone is different.
asks: Tell me about hears a comment

faq.a: Yes. Men work as nurses all over the world, caring for babies, children and adults. Caring and kindness are human skills, not boy or girl skills.
Yes. Women design bridges, robots, rockets and phones. For example, Indian scientist Tessy Thomas helped lead the Agni missile projects, and many engineering students today are women.
asks: Tell me about meets real people

faq.q: Why do some jobs have more men or more women?
faq.a: Mostly because of history, stereotypes and who people saw doing the job when growing up. This is changing as more people see role models of every gender in every job.
asks: Tell me about any job is open

facts: Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union became the first woman in space on 16 June 1963.
Tessy Thomas, an Indian scientist at DRDO, is often called the "Missile Woman of India" for her leading role in the Agni missile projects.

quiz.say: "Only girls can be dancers." What kind of idea is this?
quiz.show: "Only girls can be dancers" is a…
quiz.why: It is a fixed idea that an activity belongs to one gender, which is a stereotype.

wrong.0: Many men are dancers, so it is not a fact.
wrong.2: No law says only girls can dance.
